In the first 20 minutes of the match, both sides were already playing with plenty of fire and brimstone. After the water break, players from each team received yellow cards — England's midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina's centre-back Lisandro Martínez. By half-time, every whistle was met with cheers from fans backing their side and jeers at the opposition for any fouls.

The first half ended in a draw, but after the sides switched ends in the second half, England's Anthony Gordon received a pass in the 55th minute and opened the scoring against Argentina, going 1-0 up. England fans around the ground immediately erupted in celebration.

After falling behind, Argentina immediately pushed forward in response. Within 10 minutes, they launched three attacks down the right with crosses into the box, all of which were cleared, drawing sighs from many Argentina supporters. It was not until the 85th minute that Enzo Fernández headed in a pass from Messi to level the score at 1-1, sending Argentina fans into a frenzy of celebration, drumming and horn-blowing.

In stoppage time in the 92nd minute, Messi provided the assist for Lautaro Martínez to score the winner against England, sending Argentina through to another final to contest the World Cup trophy against Spain. Argentina fans around the ground once again went wild. When the final whistle blew, supporters continued to embrace and celebrate, with some holding up a cardboard cutout of Messi's face from inside the mall.

Argentina fan Ah Ho said he has been a fan of Messi since the latter first came through at Barcelona. Wearing the 'two-star' Argentina number 10 shirt, he said this World Cup is Messi's last, and the team is also defending their title. Messi's and the team's campaign has sparked debate at this tournament, but Ah Ho believes that rather than getting bogged down arguing over refereeing standards in every match, one should cherish the remaining time of Messi playing for the national team. With a laugh, he said he chose to stay up late at the mall to watch with other fans 'while I'm still young enough to handle it', saying the atmosphere beats watching at home — and the result went his way, with Argentina reaching the final.

England fans had been chanting 'Football's coming home!' at this tournament, but failed to bring football home once again. Declan, who is studying in the UK, came back to Hong Kong during the summer holiday. Today he draped himself in the England flag and, throughout the fierce battle between the two sides, cheered his team on wholeheartedly with friends. He said this was his first time watching a match in a mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that fans were passionate but also respectful of each other, without any overly heated clashes.

With their side having lost, fans were inevitably disappointed. Declan — who shares a name with England midfielder Declan Rice — felt England had performed well in this match. A fan for two tournaments himself, he said bluntly: 'We've waited 60 years, waiting another four years is no big deal!'

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th in their bid to defend the title. In the third-place playoff, England will take on France on the 19th.
